`./compile.sh` reports **`compiled OK`**.

## What was produced

`tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java` — a single self-contained JUnit 4 test class (matching `junit-4.12` in `lib/`), package `org.apache.commons.lang3.time`, no external helpers, `-source 8`-clean (no diamonds/lambdas/underscored literals).

### Coverage, all derived from the `api/` Javadoc

| Area | Happy path | Boundary / error |
|---|---|---|
| **Constants** | `MILLIS_PER_*` exact values + internal multiples, `RANGE_*`/`MODIFY_*`/`SEMI_MONTH` values, `UTC_TIME_ZONE` offset/DST, public constructor | — |
| **isSameDay / isSameInstant / isSameLocalTime** | same-day-different-time, same-instant, cross-timezone instant equality vs. local-time inequality | null date **and** null calendar → `IllegalArgumentException` |
| **addX / setX** (14 methods) | add/subtract with month/year rollover and carry (ms→s→min→day); original left unmutated; distinct object | null date → `IllegalArgumentException` for every method |
| **truncate / round / ceiling** (Date, Calendar, Object) | Javadoc examples (28 Mar 2002 13:45:01.231 → HOUR/MONTH/DATE/SECOND), half-up boundaries, `SEMI_MONTH`, `truncate ≤ orig ≤ ceiling` spanning one unit, Calendar overload returns distinct object & keeps input intact | null → `IllegalArgumentException`; non-Date/Calendar → `ClassCastException` |
| **iterator** | Javadoc's flagship example (Thu Jul 4 2002 + `RANGE_MONTH_SUNDAY` → Sun Jun 30 … Sat Aug 3, 35 contiguous Calendars); all week/month range styles; Calendar focus | invalid range style, null Date/Calendar/Object → `IllegalArgumentException`; String → `ClassCastException`; `remove()` → `UnsupportedOperationException` |
| **parseDate / parseDateStrictly** | single & multi-pattern, time components, lenient rollover vs. strict rejection of the same input, Javadoc's "February 942, 1996" strict rejection | trailing text, no matching pattern, no patterns → `ParseException`; null string / null pattern array → `IllegalArgumentException` |
| **getFragmentIn{Milliseconds,Seconds,Minutes,Hours,Days}** (Date + Calendar) | every documented numeric example (538, 10538, 26110, 127, 59, …) plus the "fragment ≤ unit ⇒ 0" rule | null → `IllegalArgumentException`; unsupported fragment (`DAY_OF_WEEK`) → `IllegalArgumentException` |
| **truncatedEquals / truncatedCompareTo** (Date + Calendar) | equal/less/greater at `MONTH`, `DAY_OF_MONTH`, `HOUR_OF_DAY` granularity | null → `IllegalArgumentException` |

Tests pin the default timezone to UTC and locale to `Locale.US` in `@Before` (restored in `@After`) so calendar arithmetic is deterministic and DST-free. The buggy/self-contradictory `getFragmentInMinutes` + `MONTH` Javadoc examples were deliberately not asserted; the `DATE`/`DAY_OF_YEAR` fragment value (435) is instead cross-derived from the documented `getFragmentInSeconds` example.
